headline: NetEase fell 11% after revenue declined and earnings missed estimates
summary: NetEase reported a 1.8% fall in third-quarter revenue, with its core games business down 1.7%, and earnings per share about 12% below what analysts expected. For a company valued on steady growth in games, a quarter of shrinking sales was enough for a double-digit drop.
why: NetEase published third-quarter results on November 19. Net revenues were RMB27.9 billion, about $4.2 billion, down 1.8% from a year earlier. Games and related services, which make up more than 80% of the business, fell 1.7% to RMB22.9 billion. Earnings per share were roughly 12% below the analyst consensus.

The decline was spread across the group: the Youdao education unit fell 12.3% and Cloud Music slipped 0.9%, with only the smaller ‘innovative businesses’ segment growing. Gross profit still rose 4.8% and operating expenses fell 5.4%, so NetEase is earning more on each sale, but it is selling less.

NetEase’s release pointed to sustained engagement in established titles such as Fantasy Westward Journey, Identity V and Where Winds Meet. What investors did not find in the numbers was a new hit large enough to offset older games maturing.
context: Game companies’ revenue moves with their release schedule, so a single weak quarter does not by itself say the franchise is in decline. NetEase remains highly profitable, with non-GAAP net income of RMB9.2 billion in the quarter, and it declared a dividend of $0.585 per ADS.
